questions.topic: The right to stop work in a dangerous situation
questions.stem: Explain why leaving the site without informing anyone can defeat a safety stoppage claim.

answer.exemplar: The right requires informing the employer; leaving without notice looks like unauthorised absence rather than a protected safety stoppage.

questions.explanation: Notice is required. Leaving silently resembles absence, not protected stoppage.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a union negotiates and who it covers

stimulus.body: The union proposes changes to on-call allowances and weekend rest days for the whole support unit.

questions.stem: Which proposal is a normal subject of union negotiation?

options.text: On-call allowances and weekend rest days.
The colour of the support team's logo.
The brand of laptops used.
The layout of the car park.

questions.explanation: On-call allowances and rest days are core working conditions and normal negotiation subjects.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The ordinary route of a disagreement about a dismissal
questions.stem: Who ultimately decides a dismissal dispute if conciliation fails?

options.text: The employer alone.
The union alone.
The judge at the hearing.
The team by vote.

questions.explanation: The judge decides after conciliation fails. Neither employer, union, nor team decides.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Adjusting a post to a health condition
questions.learningObjective: Identify an adjustment that changes duties
questions.stem: A frontend developer with a repetitive strain condition is moved from typing-heavy tasks to review and mentoring. Is this an adjustment?

options.text: No, because the title did not change.
No, because pay should drop.
Yes, duties changed to fit the condition.
Yes, but only if the developer agrees to resign later.

questions.explanation: Changing duties to fit the condition is a valid adjustment. Title or pay changes are not required.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The usual basis of a promotion
questions.stem: Explain why popularity among peers is a weak basis for promotion.

answer.exemplar: Popularity does not measure competence or results, so promoting on it risks rewarding likability rather than contribution.

questions.explanation: Popularity is not competence. Merit and results are the sound basis.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a performance review has to produce

stimulus.body: The review file gives a rating and a training budget but sets no goals for the coming year.

questions.stem: What is missing from this review?

options.text: A development plan with future goals.
A disciplinary warning.
A pay rise decision.
A team announcement.

questions.explanation: Future goals are part of the development plan. A rating and budget alone are insufficient.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The procedure that protects an employee facing dismissal
questions.learningObjective: Identify a defect in the interview
questions.stem: An employer holds a preliminary interview but refuses to let the employee speak. Is the procedure compliant?

options.text: Yes, because the meeting happened.
Yes, if a letter is sent later.
No, the employee must be able to respond.
No, because the union was absent.

questions.explanation: The interview must allow the employee to respond. A meeting without that right is defective.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a rotating shift post involves
questions.learningObjective: Apply the definition to a hybrid schedule
questions.stem: A developer works three days on-site and two days remotely but always 09:00 to 17:00. Is this a rotating shift post?

options.text: Yes, because the workplace changes.
Yes, because the team is hybrid.
No, the working hours never change.
No, because remote work is forbidden.

questions.explanation: Hybrid location does not change hours. Fixed hours mean no rotation.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The right to stop work in a dangerous situation
questions.stem: Explain why a sparking power strip qualifies for the safety stoppage right.

answer.exemplar: A sparking power strip presents serious and imminent danger of fire or shock, so stopping work is protected under the safety right.

questions.explanation: Sparks present serious and imminent danger, qualifying for protection.
